verdict: Leidos grew revenue 4% to $4.6B and net income 12% to $413M, powered by a 32% jump in its Homeland business, and raised its full-year guidance for the third straight quarter.

segments.name: Intelligence & Digital
segments.note: Intelligence-community mission support and digital services — up 1% on recent contract awards and expanded scope, partly offset by declines in some federal civilian IT programs.

segments.name: Health
segments.note: Managed health services and health IT for government — down 12% on expected program shifts and lower volumes, though still the most profitable segment at a 22.5% operating margin.

segments.name: Homeland
segments.note: Air traffic management and power-grid engineering — up 32% on strong demand plus $142M from the ENTRUST Solutions acquisition.

segments.name: Defense
segments.note: Defense technology — air defense, sensing and C5ISR systems — up 3%.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Corporate and selling costs — down from $290M a year ago on disciplined cost management.

opex.name: Acquisition & restructuring costs
opex.note: Costs tied to recent strategic corporate transactions, including the ENTRUST Solutions deal.

otherDetail: Net non-operating expense of $64M after equity earnings: interest expense, net of $67M and $4M of other expense, partly offset by $7M of equity earnings from joint ventures. Leidos reports those equity earnings inside operating income (reported operating income was $553M); they are shown here with other income so the chart foots.

takeaways.title: Homeland is booming
takeaways.text: Homeland revenue jumped 32% to $1,024M on air traffic management and power-distribution engineering demand, including $142M from the ENTRUST Solutions acquisition — more than offsetting Health's 12% decline.

takeaways.title: Adjusted EPS rose 19%
takeaways.text: Non-GAAP EPS was $3.62, up 19% (GAAP $3.28, up 16%). A lower effective tax rate — helped by a bigger federal research credit — flattered both figures, alongside improved program performance.

takeaways.title: A deep backlog
takeaways.text: Total backlog reached $49.6B at quarter-end, about 2.7 times annual revenue, giving Leidos long visibility on future work — $11.1B of it already funded.

oneTimers: GAAP results include $12M of costs associated with recent strategic corporate transactions (the acquisition, integration and restructuring line). Excluding these and items like amortization of acquired intangibles, non-GAAP net income was $455M ($3.62 per share) versus $413M ($3.28) GAAP.
footerNote: Leidos' fiscal third quarter ended October 2, 2026. Leidos reports $7M of equity earnings from joint ventures inside operating income (reported operating income $553M); this chart shows that $7M alongside other income so the money flow foots, which puts chart operating profit at $546M. Net income is the consolidated $413M; $410M was attributable to Leidos common stockholders, with $3M to noncontrolling interests. Leidos realigned its segments at the start of fiscal 2026 (Intelligence & Digital, Health, Homeland, Defense); prior-year figures are recast.
